output.summary: KEP-3668 proposes subdividing the NodePort service port range into a reserved block for static port assignment and a dynamic block, so users can create NodePort Services with static ports with less risk of conflict. The KEP is implemented and stable.
output.rationale: Users need well-known, predefined NodePort numbers, but dynamic allocation can already have taken a port before a static NodePort Service is created. The design splits the NodePort range so static and dynamic allocations do not collide, modeled on KEP-3070 for Cluster IPs. The stated goal is to allow a static NodePort with less risk of port conflict, and the non-goals exclude changing the allocator implementation or adding new configuration flags.

alternatives.option: Keep a single shared NodePort range for static and dynamic allocation
alternatives.why_not: The summary notes that without a split, there is no way to know before creating a static NodePort Service whether another dynamic NodePort has already taken the port.
Listed as a non-goal of the KEP.

alternatives.option: Add new configuration options or flags
alternatives.why_not: Listed as a non-goal of the KEP.

evidence.quote: The NodePort Service port range can be logically subdivided to avoid the risk of conflict between NodePort that use static and dynamic port allocation.

The idea is mostly the same with [Reserve Service IP Ranges (KEP-3070)](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-network/3070-reserved-service-ip-range#release-signoff-checklist) did.
Currently, there is no possibility, before creating a NodePort Service with a static port, to know if the port has been chosen already by any other NodePort using dynamic allocation.
- allow to create a Service with a static NodePort with less risk of port conflict.

## Non-Goals
- changing the allocators implementation (bitmaps, ...). - add new configuration options or flags.
